01 / THE GAME THE PREMISE

A small team.
A very big world.

To a child, it's just a house. To his toys, it's the entire world.

Playtime Protocol: Innocence Lost is a story-driven 3D RPG that follows four living toys separated from the child they love. What begins as an escape from a mysterious danger becomes something far more personal: a journey through fear, trust, sacrifice, and growing up.

Every room is an expedition. Every ordinary object tells a family story. And every hero will discover that being brave is not quite the same thing as being responsible.

03 / THE JOURNEY TWO DIRECTIONS. ONE HOME.

First, they run.
Then, they return.

At the heart of the adventure is a simple idea: the same place can feel completely different when you understand what matters.

I.

THE OUTWARD JOURNEY

Find safety.
Keep moving.

A mysterious danger drives the toys away from everything familiar. The farther they travel, the more they discover how little they understand about the world.

AWAY FROM HOME →
II.

THE RETURN JOURNEY

Choose courage.
Protect home.

Escape cannot make the future certain. So they choose to turn around. The same rooms become a different kind of adventure when the toys come back to protect one another.

05 / GAMEPLAY UNDER ACTIVE DESIGN

Think together.
Fight together.

Every toy is built differently. That should change everything about how you play.

Our current combat direction explores fast, readable, turn-based tactical encounters within the 3D environment. Position, movement, objects, and the strengths of each character should all matter.

Adventure shifts between solo play, carefully chosen pairs, and the full four-toy party as the story demands. The game must work for all of them.

07 / THE CREATOR'S DOSSIER BEHIND THE ADVENTURE

The story goes
much deeper.

For readers who want more than the public-facing premise: explore the narrative rules, the parallel human story, and the full intended emotional resolution.

01What is CJ experiencing?

CJ is twelve, growing toward adolescence while his family welcomes newborn twins. His story concerns freedom, responsibility, negligence and consequences, parental sacrifice, and the changing place of his childhood toys in his life.

A non-negotiable storytelling rule: the player only sees or hears CJ's experiences when the toys can observe them from their actual locations. There are no omniscient cutaways or unrestricted glimpses into his private life.

02What is the Unknown?

The Unknown is the mysterious threat that fractures the toys' familiar world. Its thematic role is connected to uncertainty and the impossibility of making the future entirely safe. Its true appearance, origins, physical rules, enemies, and final degree of explanation have not been decided.

Its tension should not require making the entire game a horror game. Scale, framing, pauses, and recognizable domestic spaces are essential to its presentation.

03How do the toys change?

Jayze learns to stop confusing capability with good leadership. Kip learns to trust his own decisions. Rallo discovers that courage means acting in spite of fear. Captain Crusher—whose personal name, Jonnie, is revealed on the return—learns to trust others without surrendering her independence.

Two separate kinds of party separation reinforce their arcs: an early forced scattering and a later deliberate split into Jayze/Jonnie and Kip/Rallo. On the journey home, the same characters make different decisions that prove what they have learned.

04The intended ending FULL STORY SPOILERS

After reaching the alley and receiving help from the grandparents' heirlooms, the toys realize that running farther will never make the future certain. They independently decide to return and protect CJ and the family alongside the older household belongings.

After the climactic defense, the toys recognize that CJ is growing up and may no longer need them in the same way. The victory turns briefly bittersweet—until the newborn twins' eventual inheritance of the toys gives them a new purpose. Illustrated cinematic stills during the credits show the family's lives continuing.

The loss of innocence is not the loss of love or play. It is the beginning of a more responsible kind of love.
